claim: A sourcing consultant named Eric on China posted a reel titled The 15-Cent Miracle — The Most Ruthless Supply Chain on Earth.
source_quote: A sourcing consultant who goes by "Eric on China" (@ericcrackschina) posts a reel titled "The 15-Cent Miracle — The Most Ruthless Supply Chain on Earth."

claim: Eric claims Chinese manufacturing operates profitably on under one cent of profit per unit.
source_quote: a small Chinese city dominates global manufacturing on under one cent of profit per unit

claim: Western hardware founders typically pursue 50% profit margins.
source_quote: while Western hardware founders chase 50% margins

claim: Eric sells sourcing services and uses his content for lead generation.
source_quote: Eric sells sourcing services — the reel is partly a lead-generation pitch ("send me a DM… sourcing agent… cost control").

claim: The under one cent profit per unit figure is a characterization of a business model rather than an audited accounting of a specific factory.
source_quote: The specific "under one cent of profit per unit" figure is Eric's characterisation of a model — the thin-margin, high-volume economics of commodity hardware made at immense scale — rather than an audited accounting of any one factory.

claim: Chinese manufacturing wages rose sharply between 2005 and 2016.
source_quote: Chinese manufacturing wages rose sharply between 2005 and 2016

claim: By the mid-2010s, Chinese manufacturing wages had surpassed manufacturing wages in Mexico and Brazil.
source_quote: by the mid-2010s they had surpassed manufacturing wages in Mexico and Brazil

claim: China retained and grew its manufacturing dominance despite rising wages.
source_quote: yet China retained and grew its manufacturing dominance.

claim: Shenzhen, Dongguan, and Yiwu are cities with dense networks of suppliers and component makers.
source_quote: Cities like Shenzhen, Dongguan, and Yiwu concentrate dense networks of suppliers, component makers, toolmakers, and assemblers within driving distance of one another.

claim: Cluster density enables prototyping and iteration in days rather than months.
source_quote: a designer can prototype, get a custom part, revise it, and re-test in days, not months.

claim: Cluster density is the most-cited factor by engineers and analysts working in the system.
source_quote: Cluster density is the single most-cited factor by the engineers and analysts who actually work in this system.

claim: The micro-margin model operates by multiplying tiny unit profit across tens of millions of units.
source_quote: the unit profit is tiny, but multiplied across tens of millions of units it is enormous in aggregate.

claim: Automation has been substituted for rising labor costs in Chinese manufacturing.
source_quote: automation has substituted for the rising wage bill

claim: China uses export-tax rebates and coordinated planning to lower costs for global market access.
source_quote: World-class ports, roads, and power, plus export-tax rebates and coordinated planning, lower the all-in cost of getting goods to global markets.

claim: Low value-add, labor-intensive manufacturing has been migrating to Vietnam and Bangladesh.
source_quote: Low value-add, labour-intensive manufacturing has been migrating to lower-wage neighbours (Vietnam, Bangladesh) as Chinese wages rose

claim: China is increasingly competitive in medium- and higher-value manufacturing rather than the most labor-intensive tiers.
source_quote: What remains competitive in China is increasingly medium- and higher-value manufacturing, where ecosystem depth, skilled labour, and integration matter more than wage rates.

claim: Chinese manufacturing competitiveness is partly supported by subsidies and state support that distort true cost.
source_quote: subsidies and state support that distort true cost

claim: Rebuilding Western manufacturing depth would take decades rather than tariff cycles.
source_quote: rebuilding that depth takes decades, not tariff cycles.
